tools.description:
Retrieve 1-2 cited examples from recorded demonstrations, not a new plan.

        Describe the CURRENT visible scene. Use once before planning; query again only
        for an information gap/recovery. Text uses Chinese labels; Chinese queries work best.
        Raw action arrays/images stay behind read_action_reference to keep context small.

tools.name: read_action_reference
tools.description:
Expand graph_id:phase_id from a retrieved graph into historical before/action/after evidence.

        Recorded actions are world link6 deltas. When the live controller uses that same
        interface, learn their scale/orientation/gripper timing, but adapt to CURRENT images.
        An absolute TCP controller requires a coordinate conversion; never blindly replay rows.
        Images are explicitly historical and must not replace current feedback.
        section=end selects the final window of a phase, useful for release/withdrawal.
        section=close/open selects a window around the first gripper command crossing
        0.5 in this phase. Use close for grasp posture; phase starts can be far away.
        If no such event exists, the response explicitly falls back to phase start.
        Default summaries include displacement/gripper timing; raw arrays are optional.

tools.name: observe
tools.description:
Current RGB and measured fingertip TCP state; no simulation step or object ground truth.

        Set calibration=true initially for camera ray/plane calculations. World z is height in meters.
        Reuse fixed head calibration; moving wrist extrinsics need refreshing after movement.

tools.name: record_plan
execute_chunk
tools.description:
Submit 1-24 NEW action rows in the SAME format as historical action references.

            Each row: [L dx,dy,dz,rx,ry,rz,gripper, R dx,dy,dz,rx,ry,rz,gripper].
            EE=link6, not TCP. World translation meters, WORLD ROTVEC radians (not Euler).
            Start from current action_state EE poses. Accumulate subsequent rows from
            PREVIOUS REQUESTED targets. Gripper 0=closed/1=open, held per row. 25Hz.
            Per-arm limits per row: translation norm<=0.035m; rotation norm<=0.35rad.
            Prefer segments=[{delta:[14 numbers],repeat:N},...] for repeated rows.
            Segments expand EXACTLY to actions, with <=24 total rows; do not supply both.
            To avoid calculating deltas, use targets=[{steps:N,left:{tcp_xyz:[x,y,z],
            quaternion_wxyz:[w,x,y,z],gripper:0},right:{...}},...]. Select ONLY one
            of actions, segments, targets. Omitted arms/fields hold previous targets.
            Targets linearly interpolate LINK6 translation and world rotation to the
            requested fingertip endpoints (local +X 0.145m); this is not straight TCP
            motion during rotation. Gripper applies from the segment's first row.
            Total steps<=24; same delta limits. No IK/grasp/fold planner is added.
            Both arms execute together. Large measured tracking error (>4cm) stops tail.
            No implicit grasp verification. Inspect returned RGB and revise from new state.
            When the object is released and fingers clear, return_home=true returns
            both arms to their initial joint poses, satisfying the task's final requirement.

tools.name: measure_mug_geometry
tools.description:
Optional RGB/calibration geometry, zero control steps; no holding or task-success sensor.

        Select pixels yourself from current images; matching the same physical point
        across cameras is your responsibility. camera='head', camera2='wrist_r'
        by default; either may also be wrist_l. Pixel arguments accept [u,v],
        [[u,v],...] or 'u,v;u,v' text, using ORIGINAL image coordinates.
        surface: pixels plus matching pixels2, OR your measured horizontal height z.
        stereo_guide: pixels, optional pixels2 -> epipolar correspondence diagnostics.
        peg_measure: tip/root in camera, tip2/root2 in camera2, and edges and/or
        edges2 on BOTH long silhouette sides -> tip, root, root-to-tip axis and radius.
        aperture: 4-32 matched INNER boundary points rim/rim2, center=[u,v] in
        camera -> center, plane normal and conservative clear radius. It assumes
        a planar opening; a solid surface or wrong correspondence is not certified.
        Failed/weak measurements change no robot state. These tools are optional;
        choose new views, direct triangulation or another approach as appropriate.

tools.name: hold_joints
tools.description:
Hold both MEASURED arm joint positions for 1-24 native steps, optionally changing one gripper.

        No Cartesian IK, object sensing or grasp guarantee. Omit arm/gripper to
        settle with both commands preserved. Inspect RGB after closing/releasing.
        Each dispatch counts toward the native budget. A plan is required.

tools.name: python_cell
tools.description:
Persistent Python: variables/functions/imports survive cells; stdout, last value, errors and fresh RGB/state return.

        np, math, Rotation, Image, display(image), robo are defined. Pure computation
        is isolated from host/network/simulator; no hidden object or reward state.
        robo.state() includes current camera K,T and action_state; robo.image(camera)
        returns PIL RGB; robo.show(camera) displays it. Save snapshots with images.
        pixel_to_plane(snapshot,camera,[u,v],z) uses YOUR height assumption.
        triangulate([(snapshot,camera,[u,v]),...]) returns xyz and reprojection error
        for the same STATIC visible point; matching features remains your decision.
        tcp_pose(snapshot,arm) -> (xyz, scipy Rotation); quaternion convention wxyz.
        The same pure geometry helpers also accept the robo. prefix, with identical
        arguments: robo.pixel_to_plane(...), robo.triangulate(...), robo.tcp_pose(...).

        robo.move(arm,xyz=None,quaternion=None,gripper=None,steps=16,subgoal=...,
        expected_feedback=...) requests 1-24 straight TCP samples with interpolated
        orientation. xyz=None holds current TCP while turning. Omitted gripper holds
        its command. Original native IK/limits/step budget apply; no grasp planner.
        robo.grip(arm,value,steps=8) holds measured arm JOINTS while changing one gripper,
        bypassing Cartesian IK. robo.hold(steps=8) holds both joints/gripper commands.
        Values are COMMANDS, not holding sensors; inspect RGB after contact.
        robo.execute(subgoal=...,expected_feedback=...,actions/segments/targets=...)
        wraps execute_chunk; robo.home() wraps return_home after you withdraw clear.
        A move returns execution and current_observation plus pose target_error.
        IK rejection, truncation or >4cm last-row tracking error stops further motion
        in this cell. Rejected rows consume no steps and change neither gripper.
        The native IK continuity limit is 0.25rad per joint; revise the approach
        or use smaller increments from the latest measured pose. Read RGB and revise in a NEW
        cell. End cells at uncertain contacts, grasp/lift and release; combine
        predictable free motion/calculations in functions. Do not treat pose error
        as grasp success. 120-second compute deadline; completed motions persist
        after errors, so never blindly rerun a failed cell. record_plan still precedes movement.
        

        Hang-mug helpers: robo.measure(command, **arguments) calls the optional
        measure_mug_geometry tool with the same arguments and zero action steps.
        robo.move_feature(arm,source,target,quaternion=None,gripper=None,steps=16,
        subgoal=...,expected_feedback=...) moves a chosen CURRENT world feature
        along a line while rotating. source/target are world xyz, quaternion is wxyz.
        It accounts for the feature offset from TCP at every intermediate sample;
        target=source rotates about the selected feature. This assumes rigid grasp,
        not collision-free motion or observed feature tracking. Read RGB after contact.
        It shares execute_chunk validation, 1-24-row dispatches, plan requirement,
        native step budget and stop-on-truncation with robo.move.

tools.name: python_cell
tools.description:
Persistent Python: variables/functions/imports survive cells; stdout, last value, errors and fresh RGB/state return.

        np, math, Rotation, Image, display(image), robo are defined. Pure computation
        is isolated from host/network/simulator; no hidden object or reward state.
        robo.state() includes current camera K,T and action_state; robo.image(camera)
        returns PIL RGB; robo.show(camera) displays it. Save snapshots with images.
        pixel_to_plane(snapshot,camera,[u,v],z) uses YOUR height assumption.
        triangulate([(snapshot,camera,[u,v]),...]) returns xyz and reprojection error
        for the same STATIC visible point; matching features remains your decision.
        tcp_pose(snapshot,arm) -> (xyz, scipy Rotation); quaternion convention wxyz.
        The same pure geometry helpers also accept the robo. prefix, with identical
        arguments: robo.pixel_to_plane(...), robo.triangulate(...), robo.tcp_pose(...).

        robo.move(arm,xyz=None,quaternion=None,gripper=None,steps=16,subgoal=...,
        expected_feedback=...) requests 1-24 straight TCP samples with interpolated
        orientation. xyz=None holds current TCP while turning. Omitted gripper holds
        its command. Original native IK/limits/step budget apply; no grasp planner.
        robo.grip(arm,value,steps=8) holds measured arm JOINTS while changing one gripper,
        bypassing Cartesian IK. robo.hold(steps=8) holds both joints/gripper commands.
        Values are COMMANDS, not holding sensors; inspect RGB after contact.
        robo.execute(subgoal=...,expected_feedback=...,actions/segments/targets=...)
        wraps execute_chunk; robo.home() wraps return_home after you withdraw clear.
        A move returns execution and current_observation plus pose target_error.
        IK rejection, truncation or >4cm last-row tracking error stops further motion
        in this cell. Rejected rows consume no steps and change neither gripper.
        The native IK continuity limit is 0.25rad per joint; revise the approach
        or use smaller increments from the latest measured pose. Read RGB and revise in a NEW
        cell. End cells at uncertain contacts, grasp/lift and release; combine
        predictable free motion/calculations in functions. Do not treat pose error
        as grasp success. 120-second compute deadline; completed motions persist
        after errors, so never blindly rerun a failed cell. record_plan still precedes movement.
        

        Hang-mug helpers: robo.measure(command, **arguments) calls the optional
        measure_mug_geometry tool with the same arguments and zero action steps.
        robo.move_feature(arm,source,target,quaternion=None,gripper=None,steps=16,
        subgoal=...,expected_feedback=...) moves a chosen CURRENT world feature
        along a line while rotating. source/target are world xyz, quaternion is wxyz.
        It accounts for the feature offset from TCP at every intermediate sample;
        target=source rotates about the selected feature. This assumes rigid grasp,
        not collision-free motion or observed feature tracking. Read RGB after contact.
        It shares execute_chunk validation, 1-24-row dispatches, plan requirement,
        native step budget and stop-on-truncation with robo.move.
